summary: The non-GAIA version is a compact code-only Python implementation. It addresses the six requirements with direct classes and in-memory state, including location history, behavior rules, health checks, reminders, and appointment scheduling. Its main weakness is architectural: the named agents are ordinary classes coordinated through shared globals rather than a defined multi-agent communication model.

findings.description: The implementation contains concrete classes or methods for all six requirements.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/pet_management_system.py defines LocationTrackingAgent at line 61, BehaviorControlAgent at line 100, HealthMonitoringAgent at line 129, VetAppointmentReminderAgent at line 174, and VetAppointmentSchedulingAgent.schedule_appointment at line 218.

findings.description: Location saving is implemented with both current location and history.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/pet_management_system.py:77-81 initializes location_history, appends location_data, and sets current_location.

findings.description: The system uses shared module-level dictionaries instead of explicit agent messages, protocols, or request/response contracts, so communication correctness is not specified.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/pet_management_system.py:6-8 defines global pets and vet_appointments; the agent classes then read and mutate pets directly, for example lines 77-81 and 232-235.

findings.description: Reminder checking silently skips malformed appointment dates, which can hide reminder failures.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/pet_management_system.py:197-208 catches Exception during date parsing and continues.

findings.description: The system is an in-memory simulation rather than a persistent application, so records and appointments disappear after process exit.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/pet_management_system.py:6-8 stores all core data in module dictionaries, and line 292 defines run_simulation.

findings.description: Some dependencies are unpinned, which weakens reproducibility.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/requirements.txt lists langchain, langchain-community, and langchain-core without exact versions.

logical_inconsistencies: The code names several classes as agents, but no inter-agent protocol, message schema, or orchestration contract is defined.
vet_appointments is declared globally but appointment scheduling stores appointments under pets[pet_id], leaving the global appointment store unused.
implementation_risks: Shared mutable globals make behavior order-dependent and unsuitable for concurrent or multi-user execution.
Malformed appointment dates can suppress reminders without surfacing an error.
All data is in memory, so pet records, locations, health data, and appointments are lost on restart.
Unpinned LangChain dependencies can cause installation drift.
